conceptBreakdown.heading: 1. Chemical Fractionation Protocol & Acid Pools
conceptBreakdown.title: 1. Chemical Fractionation Protocol & Acid Pools

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Acid-soluble = Micromolecules (<1000 Da, cytoplasm). Acid-insoluble = Macromolecules (>1000 Da) PLUS Lipids (trapped as insoluble membrane vesicles).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
CHEMICAL FRACTIONATION PROTOCOL
                                    │
  Living Tissue (Liver / Leaf) ──► Grind in 5% Trichloroacetic Acid ($\text{Cl}_3\text{CCOOH}$)
                                    │
  Filter through Cheesecloth / Cheesecloth mesh ──► TWO FRACTIONS
                                    │
         ┌──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                     ▼
ACID-SOLUBLE POOL (Filtrate)                          ACID-INSOLUBLE POOL (Retentate)
├── Micromolecules ($MW < 1000\text{ Da}$)            ├── Macromolecules ($MW > 1000\text{ Da}$)
├── Monosaccharides, Amino Acids,                     ├── Proteins, Polysaccharides,
│   Nucleotides, Organic Acids                        │   Nucleic Acids
└── Represents Cytoplasmic Composition                └── **LIPIDS** ($MW \approx 800\text{ Da}$) [Membrane vesicles]
conceptBreakdown.content:
All living organisms are composed of carbon-based chemical compounds called **Biomolecules**.

### Analytical Fractions
1. **Acid-Soluble Pool (Filtrate)**: Contains low-molecular-weight compounds ($18\text{--}800\text{ Da}$) representing the cytoplasmic solute composition (monosaccharides, amino acids, nucleotides, organic acids).
2. **Acid-Insoluble Fraction (Retentate)**: Contains polymeric macromolecules ($MW > 10,000\text{ Da}$) including proteins, polysaccharides, and nucleic acids.
3. **The Lipid Paradox (CRITICAL NEST TRAP)**: Lipids have molecular weights $<800\text{ Da}$ and are structurally **micromolecules**. However, during tissue grinding, cellular membranes fragment into insoluble water-impermeable lipid vesicles that cannot pass through the filter mesh, partitioning into the acid-insoluble retentate.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.1 Primary vs. Secondary Metabolites
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.1 Primary vs. Secondary Metabolites
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
METABOLITE CLASSES
                                         │
         ┌───────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                               ▼
  PRIMARY METABOLITES                                             SECONDARY METABOLITES
  ├── Direct role in basic physiological processes                ├── No direct primary role in organism growth/dev
  ├── Ubiquitous across all living taxa                           ├── Taxon-specific (plants, fungi, microbes)
  └── Examples: Amino acids, Sugars, Nucleotides,                 └── Examples: Alkaloids, Antibiotics, Pigments,
      Lipids, Coenzymes                                               Toxins, Lectins, Gums, Rubber
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Primary Metabolites**: Ubiquitous molecules with direct, identifiable roles in normal physiological processes (amino acids, sugars, nucleotides, lipids, chlorophyll).
• **Secondary Metabolites**: Taxon-specific ecological, defensive, or specialized chemical products in plants, fungi, and microbes.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Secondary Metabolites Taxonomic Matrix
conceptBreakdown.title: Secondary Metabolites Taxonomic Matrix
conceptBreakdown.content:
| Secondary Metabolite Category | Specific Representative Compounds | Biological / Economic Significance |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Pigments** | Carotenoids ($\alpha/\beta$-Carotene, Lutein), Anthocyanins | Photosynthetic accessory pigments; floral attractants |
| **Alkaloids** | **Morphine**, **Codeine**, Quinine, Nicotine, Strychnine | Narcotic analgesics; plant defense compounds |
| **Terpenoids** | Monoterpenes, Sesquiterpenes, **Camphor**, Citronellal | Volatile essential oils; herbivore deterrents |
| **Toxins** | **Abrin** (from *Abrus precatorius*), **Ricin** (from *Ricinus communis*) | Ribosome-inactivating toxic proteins |
| **Lectins** | **Concanavalin A** (from *Canavalia ensiformis*) | Carbohydrate-binding agglutinating proteins |
| **Drugs / Pharmaceuticals** | **Vinblastine**, **Vincristine** (from *Catharanthus*), **Curcumin** (from *Curcuma*) | Anti-cancer mitotic spindle inhibitors; anti-inflammatory |
| **Polymeric Substances** | **Rubber** (*Hevea* latex), **Gums**, **Cellulose** | Industrial polymers, structural cell walls |
| **Essential Oils** | Lemon grass oil, Eucalyptus oil, Rose oil | Perfumery, antimicrobial agents |
